a_raw: {"translation":"Target names, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every function f from finite lists of elements of X to Y, and every natural number T, there exists a system N of type S1 X Y with exactly T coordinates and no directed cycle of dependencies, such that for every list xs of elements of X, if xs has length at most T, then N’s output on xs equals f(xs). A dependency edge from m to n means that there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every coordinate other than m, and a single input x, for which the update at n gives different values on the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable. No coordinate may have a chain of one or more such edges back to itself, so self-edges are forbidden too. To obtain the output, N starts in its specified initial assignment, reads xs from left to right, updates all coordinates at each step from the same previous assignment and current input, and applies its output function to the final assignment. The coordinate state types need not be finite. N may depend on X, Y, f, and T, but the same N must work for all lists of length at most T, including the empty list. No agreement with f is required on longer lists. T may be zero, in which case N must have zero coordinates and match f on the empty list."}
translation: Target names, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every function f from finite lists of elements of X to Y, and every natural number T, there exists a system N of type S1 X Y with exactly T coordinates and no directed cycle of dependencies, such that for every list xs of elements of X, if xs has length at most T, then N’s output on xs equals f(xs). A dependency edge from m to n means that there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every coordinate other than m, and a single input x, for which the update at n gives different values on the two assignments. The assignments need not be reachable. No coordinate may have a chain of one or more such edges back to itself, so self-edges are forbidden too. To obtain the output, N starts in its specified initial assignment, reads xs from left to right, updates all coordinates at each step from the same previous assignment and current input, and applies its output function to the final assignment. The coordinate state types need not be finite. N may depend on X, Y, f, and T, but the same N must work for all lists of length at most T, including the empty list. No agreement with f is required on longer lists. T may be zero, in which case N must have zero coordinates and match f on the empty list.

divergences.description: P-D51b attributes universal approximation to recurrent neural networks, not feedforward networks. The target requires acyclicity; it is P-H11, not P-D51b, that supplies the feedforward claim.

The target requires exact equality on every history within the horizon. P-D51b says approximation to any desired accuracy, which need not yield any one network with zero error. Lean has no notion of error or accuracy here. Exact equality fits P-H11’s word “implement,” but is not a translation of P-D51b’s approximation claim.

An S1 unit can have an arbitrary state type, and its update and the readout can be arbitrary mathematical functions, with no computability requirement. For example, units can retain the inputs and the readout can apply f itself to the recovered history. Representation in this model does not establish implementation by neural units of the kind discussed in the passages.

Neither passage gives a network-size bound. The target adds that exactly T state coordinates suffice, independently of f and the input and output types, without counting the complexity of the readout. This is a sufficiency claim, not a claim that T units are necessary.

The network may depend on T and need not agree with f on any longer history. Thus the target does not assert that one network implements the whole temporal function f. P-H11 does not state this cutoff or distinguish a network for each horizon from one network for all horizons.

The target gives “when time plays a role” a specific discrete-time meaning: inputs arrive one list element at a time, units update synchronously from an initial state, and the final state is read out. Feedforwardness is acyclicity of functional dependencies between updates. P-H11 does not prescribe these modeling choices.

judgement.summary: The target expresses the declared bounded-history analogue: quantifying over total list functions loses no bounded-history functions, since each can be extended using its value on the empty list. The divergence is from the passages, which do not give this exact T-unit representation claim for abstract acyclic systems.
